ros2-mobile-robots/exercises-exercise-1:
• handle_scan() is called with parentheses in create_subscription, which raises a TypeError (no scan argument); pass handle_scan.
  • The callback returns the message; it must call publisher.publish(Bool(data=True)).
  • build_node() does not return the node; add return node.
ros2-mobile-robots/exercises-exercise-2: 0.5 usable. -inf not usable: too close to measure. NaN not usable: invalid. 3.5 usable, because it equals range_max and only values above it are discarded. 3.6 discarded: above range_max. +inf not usable: nothing detected in range. 0.1 discarded: below range_min.
ros2-mobile-robots/exercises-exercise-3:
1. linear.x = -0.1, angular.z = 0.0.
  2. linear.x = 0.0, angular.z = -0.4.
  3. linear.x = 0.0, angular.z = 0.0.
  4. Drive forward at 0.15 m/s while turning left at 0.3 rad/s: a curve to the left.
  5. 90 degrees is π/2 rad, so (π/2) / 0.4 ≈ 3.93 seconds.
ros2-mobile-robots/exercises-exercise-4: Rows: 0.24 lamp on; 0.25 lamp on ("or closer" includes the limit); 0.26 lamp off; 1.00 lamp off; NaN lamp on (the rule says so). Finite readings need <=. The limit 0.25 is stored exactly as float32, so a reading of exactly 0.25 really equals the limit.
ros2-mobile-robots/math-exercises-for-ro:
Question 1: Index and angle

  1. −1.5 + 4 × 0.25 = −0.5 rad.
  2. Index 12: −1.5 + 12 × 0.25 = +1.5 rad.
  3. Index 6, because −1.5 + 6 × 0.25 = 0.0.
  4. (0.6 + 1.5) / 0.25 = 8.4, so index 8, at +0.5 rad.
  5. (1.9 + 1.5) / 0.25 = 13.6, which is past the last index (12). The direction is outside the sweep: report that, rather than using the last reading.

Question 2: Wheel speeds

v_right = 0.10 + (−0.40 × 0.30 / 2) = 0.04 m/s and v_left = 0.10 − (−0.40 × 0.30 / 2) = 0.16 m/s. The left wheel is faster, so the robot curves to the right, as negative angular.z says.
